newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Thirteen feared dead in Karachi building collapse.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen feared dead in Karachi building collapse.

text.p: Pakistan rescue teams abandoned their search for victims of a Karachi building collapse on Thursday and said the final death toll was 13.
A total of 22 people were in the building on Wednesdayh when it collapsed. Nine survived with injuries.

"There are no more survivors. We have retrived nine injured and seven dead since yesterday and according to our estimate another six dead bodies are under the debris," a senior official of the Karachi Fire Brigade told reporters.
The official said the debris was being cleared with bulldozers and cranes after all agencies involved in the rescue operation agreed there were no more people alive.
Rescue workers said initially that up to 45 labourers could have been inside the Faiza Heights apartment building when it collapsed on Wednesday afternoon.
"After interviewing several of the labourers working in the same vicinity we have concluded that there were only 22 people inside the building when it collapsed," the fire brigade official said.
Officials have blamed the collapse of the almost-completed four-storey block on the use of poor building materials.
Karachi's deputy inspector general of police, Mohammad Iqbal, said the project supervisor had been arrested and police were searching for the builders and the architect.

Karachi commissioner Mir Hussain Ali, the city's top administrator, told Reuters television that a murder case had been registered against the builders and engineers, which he said would act as a deterrent to other contractors in Karachi.
"This incident took place because of defective construction and structural failure," he said. "Probably the builders were not using the proper ingredients for construction."
